result.title: Efficient VLA Reinforcement Learning via Subchunk Rollouts in Latent World Models
result.summary: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) can improve pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies through imagined experiences. However, existing VLA-MBRL methods primarily rely on large-scale image or video generation world models, incurring large computational overhead. Latent world models offer a more efficient alternative but face two challenges: compounding errors during recursive prediction and incompatibility with VLAs' visual input interfaces. In this work, we propose LS-MBPO, a lightweight residual MBRL framework that leverages latent world models to improve upon pretrained VLAs. LS-MBPO introduces two key techniques: (1) Hierarchical Forcing, which combines dense causal supervision with autoregressive feedback to mitigate compounding prediction errors; and (2) Latent Subchunk Rollouts, which leverage action chunks from a frozen VLA policy and a latent residual policy for successive subchunk refinement, bridging the gap between latent imagination and VLA policy execution. We further introduce a Progress-Conditioned Branch-Start Curriculum that progressively shifts rollout starting points from later to earlier task stages, enabling effective policy learning from short imagined rollouts. Extensive experiments on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real-world ALOHA robot show that LS-MBPO achieves superior task performance and training efficiency compared to existing methods.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LS-MBPO，用轻量 latent world model 对预训练 VLA 策略做残差式基于模型的强化学习：以 Hierarchical Forcing 结合密集因果监督与自回归反馈抑制递推预测误差累积，并通过 latent subchunk rollouts 与渐进起始点的课程从短想象轨迹中学习。
AI.relevance_reason: 机器人动作策略并非 LVR 主线，但其对 latent 递推中误差累积的密集监督与残差修正、以及利用短想象片段训练的做法，可能为 latent 推理轨迹的训练监督与状态更新提供可核查线索。
